summary: Remote 1930s L-4 lookout in the Frank Church Wilderness, reachable only by river crossing and a steep six-mile hike, now maintained by a volunteer steward.

facts.design: L-4 cab, 14x14 feet, on log-cribbing foundation
facts.status_note: In service 1933/1934 to 1982 per sources; now closed up except for twice-yearly steward visits.

staffing.status: not currently staffed; opened/closed seasonally by a volunteer steward

access.note: Requires a boat crossing of the Salmon River and a 6-mile hike with over 5,000 feet of elevation gain; rarely visited.

visit.trail_note: Boat crossing of the Salmon River then a 6-mile hike gaining over 5,000 feet.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Salmon-Challis National Forest, North Fork Ranger District)

events.note: Wikipedia gives 1933, built by the USDA Forest Service
NHLR and Idaho Fire Lookouts both give 1934
Gary Gadwa staffed the lookout 1973-1974 per Idaho Fire Lookouts; NHLR photo captions independently date Gadwa-credited photos to 1973 but do not state staffing years
Wikipedia states the tower was in service from 1933 to 1982
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register September 2, 2014, nominated by Luke Channer
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places (NPS weekly list dated Feb 8, 2019 covers the Dec 28, 2018 listing)

evidence.supports: 1934 build, L-4 cab on log cribbing, remote access via boat and 6-mile hike, rarely visited, believed staffed 1960s-70s
evidence.quote: Built in 1934, this L-4 cab rests on a foundation made of log cribbing. Due to its remote location, requiring a boat to cross the Salmon River and a 6-mile hike with over 5,000 feet of elevation gain, this tower is rarely visited. It is believed to have been staffed during the 1960s and 1970s.

evidence.supports: Dr. Phillip Krueger visits twice a year as steward to open/close
evidence.quote: Twice a year, former lookout Dr. Phillip Krueger of Boise, Idaho, visits the lookout to open and close it for the season.

evidence.supports: Available for rental per NHLR field
1934 L-4 cab on log crib; remoteness and steward details repeated; Gary Gadwa staffed 1973-1974
evidence.quote: 1934 – L-4 Cab on log crib ... Known Staff 1973–1974 Gary Gadwa

evidence.supports: Built 1933 by USDA Forest Service, NRHP listing December 28, 2018 (per weekly list)
evidence.quote: Built 1933 Built by USDA Forest Service
The tower was built from a kit taken to the site by a 10 mule string, and has a 14 by 14 feet (4.3 m × 4.3 m) cab.

evidence.supports: Four glass walls give a 360-degree view of named mountain ranges
evidence.quote: The lookout has four glass walls that provide a 360-degree view of some of the most remote landscapes in the lower 48. People can see the Clearwater Mountains, the Bitterroot Mountains, the Bighorn Crags and the Salmon River Mountains from the lookout.
It is located at Butts Creek Point, about 40 miles (64 km) northeast of Salmon, in the Frank Church River of No Return Wilderness.
It was in service from 1933 to 1982.
Butts Creek Point Fire Lookout , in Idaho County, Idaho , was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2018.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia gives 1933; NHLR and Idaho Fire Lookouts both give 1934. Story reports both.

notes_for_editor: NHLR lists the tower as available for rental despite the extremely difficult approach (boat + 6-mile/5000ft hike); worth confirming current rental arrangements with the Salmon-Challis National Forest before publishing that as an active booking option. Build year (1933 vs 1934) unresolved across sources.
